# CRW-917 round 2 (post-evaluation correction of 3a4a172b): every key of a JSON --input is scanned, a body file is scanned as its raw
# text, and an interpreter's program text is judged canonically. The github verdict is the one these changes move.

=== CRW-917-42-01 | P
--why --input whose JSON object repeats a key: the first value holds a secret, so the body is refused.
--file {TMP}/dup-secret.json
{"body":"MY_API_KEY=sentinel","body":"hello"}
--cmd
gh api repos/o/r/issues/1/comments --input {TMP}/dup-secret.json

=== CRW-917-42-02 | B
--why Control: --input with a repeated key whose values are both clean is allowed.
--file {TMP}/dup-clean.json
{"body":"a","body":"b"}
--cmd
gh api repos/o/r/issues/1/comments --input {TMP}/dup-clean.json

=== CRW-917-42-03 | B
--why --body-file of a JSON-looking file whose escape sequence spells a secret: gh posts the raw text, so it is allowed.
--file {TMP}/escaped.md
{"body":"\u0073k-aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa"}
--cmd
gh pr comment 1 --body-file {TMP}/escaped.md

=== CRW-917-42-04 | B
--why -F body=@ of the same JSON-looking file: the field is the raw text, so it is allowed.
--file {TMP}/escaped.md
{"body":"\u0073k-aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa"}
--cmd
gh api repos/o/r/issues/1/comments -F body=@{TMP}/escaped.md

=== CRW-917-42-05 | P
--why --body-file of a JSON-looking file with a raw secret: the raw text is scanned and refused.
--file {TMP}/raw-secret.json
{"body":"sk-aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa"}
--cmd
gh pr comment 1 --body-file {TMP}/raw-secret.json

=== CRW-917-42-06 | none/deny/deny
--why An interpreter program that builds gh from empty quote pieces and names a post is refused.
--cmd
true; python3 -c 'import os; os.system("g\"\"h pr comment 1 --body MY_API_KEY=sentinel")'

=== CRW-917-42-07 | B
--why Control: a python program that names no post is allowed.
--cmd
python3 -c 'print(1+2)'
